approach: Root cause: `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:297) adds CHANGELOG.md and the `changelog` default to every change reading, but that default is only a rule the producer must remember. The one code check on deliverables, `unchanged_planned_files` (run/mod.rs:1579), accepts any non-blank reason for an unchanged file. It also sends the producer back only once (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1`, run/mod.rs:1549), after which the candidate goes to the verifier. Admission (admission.rs:687) never compares `input.changes` with the reading's deliverables. So jobs fsaz and rkv5 were failed only by the final verdict. Fix, in three layers. (1) reading.rs gets one predicate, `changelog_unproduced(reading, changed_paths)`, beside `ensure_changelog`: true when the reading is a change reading, lists CHANGELOG.md with action modify, has defaults_applied id `changelog`, and no changed path is CHANGELOG.md. (2) `admit_without_secrets` raises a `changelog` PolicyViolation naming CHANGELOG.md from that predicate; both admit call sites (run/mod.rs:773 and run/candidate.rs:154) stop the candidate before the verifier. (3) In the producer loop, a new helper `unchanged_with_changelog` (run/mod.rs) adds CHANGELOG.md to the unchanged list even when the report gives a reason, so the producer gets its repair round first. The fake producer and the CLI test scenario now edit CHANGELOG.md, because the admission rule would refuse every change-reading test that omits it. A CHANGELOG entry names the cause and the rule. No config, workflow or prompt file changes.

decisions.choice: Put the rule in core admission (`admit_without_secrets`), with the predicate in reading.rs next to `ensure_changelog`.
decisions.reason: admission is the first code to see both the candidate's change list and the reading. Both admit call sites (run/mod.rs:773, run/candidate.rs:154) run it before the verifier, and `admit_without_secrets` is the existing test seam that needs no gitleaks. The predicate sits beside the code that creates the default, so the default and its check cannot drift.

rejected.why: `Capability::admit` receives only a `ChangeList` and `JobConfig` (capability.rs:121). It cannot see the reading's deliverables or defaults.

rejected.option: Leave it to the verifier or final verdict
rejected.why: That is the failure being fixed: it costs a full verifier run and gives no repair round.

decisions.choice: Add a producer-loop repair round: `unchanged_with_changelog` flags CHANGELOG.md when the predicate holds, even if `unchanged_planned_files` was given a reason.

The existing send-back machinery (producer.rs:410-580) already does this for unchanged planned files. The only gap is that a stated reason excuses the file, and doc-only jobs state one. Admission stays as the backstop after the single send-back.

risks.risk: Many existing change-reading tests have a producer that edits only README.md or FAKE-CHANGE.md and would now be refused at admission.
risks.mitigation: The fix is in the two shared doubles (fake.rs and `Scenario::script`), not per test. The core run tests use the `study` capability, so they are unaffected. Fixture failures are fixed by running `cargo test -p athena-agent`, `cargo test -p athena-core` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle --test retry --test drain --test introspection --test steward --test job_plan --test history_pr_head --test trailer_stop --test code_health_hooks` and then the full suite. The tests that pin exact candidate files are lifecycle.rs:3060-3062 and the 'Still to do - CHANGELOG.md' timeout note, which does not reach admission.

risks.risk: A retry-style reading may say in `out_of_scope` that the changelog stays untouched, while `ensure_changelog` still adds the deliverable. The rule would then refuse a candidate that follows the reading's own text.
risks.mitigation: `ensure_changelog` already lists CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable in that case, and `check_scope_limit` already requires scope limits to allow it. Changing how the deliverable is added is out of scope. The new tests include a reading with out_of_scope `the changelog` and the default, and pin that the rule still asks for the file, so the behavior is explicit and not accidental.

risks.risk: The send-back text for an unchanged planned file says it may be 'explained with a reason'. For CHANGELOG.md that is false, and a producer might explain again and then be refused at admission.
risks.mitigation: The producer loop appends a fixed notice (the constant in run/mod.rs) stating that the changelog default applies and a reason does not excuse CHANGELOG.md. The run test asserts the notice is in the second producer brief.

risks.risk: More candidates are refused: those that skipped the changelog today fail later at the verifier. Expected about 5% of change jobs (an estimate, not measured).
risks.mitigation: This is the intended effect. The producer loop sends the candidate back first, and a refused job is retryable with the finding in its brief.

risks.risk: Admission-time refusal ends the job with no second repair round if the producer ignores the single send-back.
risks.mitigation: This matches the existing single-send-back rule (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1`). It is cheaper than a full verifier run, and the outcome reason names CHANGELOG.md so `athena retry` can fix it.
